## THE LATENT HUMAN INFLUENCE FIELD {.section-slide
   background-image="../assets/branding/section_bg.png"
   background-size="contain"

---

## What Is a Latent Field?

:::: {.columns .col-center-container .text-image-columns}
::: {.column .v-center width="20%"}
- **Latent:** Not directly measurable.
- **Field:** intensity or properties can vary throughout space and or time.
- e.g., temperature
:::
::: {.column .v-center width="80%"}
![Temperature Field](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/temperature_field_volume.webp){.img-card height="800" fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

---

## Latent Human Influence Field (LHIF)

:::: {.columns .col-center-container .text-image-columns}
::: {.column .v-center width="20%"}
- **Latent:** human influence is inferred from its traces.
- **Field:** influence can vary across the sediment archive (translated into time).
- many proxies are noisy observations of a shared LHIF.
- Proxy records differ in resolution, distribution, and measurement structure.
- Joint inference needs a model linking observations to a shared process.
:::
::: {.column .v-center width="80%"}
![Theoretical LHIF](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr1.jpg){.img-card height="800" fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Site and Context

:::: {.columns .text-image-columns}
::: {.column width="20%"}

Cannonically, Koh Ker was established by Jayavarman IV in 921 CE and became the sole capital from 928–944 CE. The site represents a brief but highly distinctive phase of Khmer urbanism, political history, monumental architecture, and sculpture. But it contains a much longer sedimentary record of human activity, which can be reconstructed through the LHIF framework.

:::
::: {.column width="80%"}

![Koh Ker in Regional Context](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/kk_regional.jpeg){.img-card height="800" fig-align="center"}

:::
::::

::: notes

:::

## Pilot Study

- Eight test trenches were dug in 2024 and we have just published the first set of results.
- Paired magnetic susceptibility and ceramic abundance.
- Rapid, low-impact excavation as a potential survey strategy.

- Proxy channels linked within a causal framework.
- Depth-wise reconstructions for the pilot trenches.

## Reconstructing Human Influence

![Per Trench Data](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr5.jpg){fig-align="center" height="800" .img-card}

::: notes
Raw data per trench.
:::

---

## Ceramics Channel

:::: {.columns .text-image-columns}
::: {.column width="20%"}

**Ceramics channel across all 8 trenches.** The model captures the depth-wise variation in ceramic abundance, which serves as a proxy for human activity. The Latent influence field is inferred from the ceramics data, showing peaks corresponding to periods of increased human activity.

:::
::: {.column width="80%"}

![Ceramics Comparison](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr6.jpg){fig-align="center" height="800" .img-card}
:::
::::

::: notes

:::

---

## Magnetic Susceptibility Channel

:::: {.columns .text-image-columns}
::: {.column width="20%"}

**Magnetic susceptibility channel across all 8 trenches.** The model captures the depth-wise variation in magnetic susceptibility, which serves as a proxy for human activity. The Latent influence field is inferred from the magnetic susceptibility data, showing peaks corresponding to periods of increased human activity.

:::
::: {.column width="80%"}

![Magnetic Susceptibility Comparison](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr7.jpg){fig-align="center" height="800" .img-card}
:::

::::

---

## pXRF Channel

:::: {.columns .text-image-columns}
::: {.column width="20%"}

**pXRF channel across all 8 trenches.** We finished the planned pXRF analysis. Here we show multidimensional differences in each trench sample between the sterile bottom layers and upper sediments. As with magnetic susceptibility, we observe depth-wise variation in elemental composition, another proxy for human activity. The Latent influence field model will be updated to include this new channel along with FTIR data (which we are currently processing) and isotope data.

:::
::: {.column width="80%"}

![pXRF Comparison](assets:2026_icc11_kohker_update/pxrf_difference_by_trench_unit.webp){fig-align="center" height="800" .img-card}

:::
::::

## Pinhole Sampling

At the moment, we have a "pinhole" view of the latent human influence field. The pilot trenches provide depth-wise reconstructions, but spatial coverage is limited. Future work could expand trenching and sampling to better understand the spatial distribution of human influence across the site.

![Pinhole Sampling](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/lhif_pinhole.webp){fig-align="center" height="600" .img-card}

---
